hpi: Patient is an adult presenting several days after rescue from the slopes of Mount Doom, following the destruction of the One Ring. He reports significant thirst, greater than any he recalls previously, with improvement since oral fluids were started. Per Sam, oral intake of food has been minimal. He reports traumatic loss of the right ring finger, bitten off during the final confrontation over the Ring. He reports the prior left shoulder wound (see encounter RIV-001) is now fully resolved and has not required attention. He reports fragmented sleep, waking multiple times nightly, and describes a persistent sensation of carrying weight associated with the Ring despite its destruction, as well as an intermittent sensation of being watched, both present since before reaching the mountain and improving but not fully resolved. He minimizes these symptoms to his companion Sam, who reports ongoing concern regardless.

physical_exam.findings: Minor first-degree burns on both hands and face, from ash and heat exposure. Not deep.
Traumatic amputation of the right ring finger, wound in early healing, no signs of active infection. Left shoulder (prior Weathertop wound) fully resolved, no findings.
Alert; oriented to person and place, uncertain of exact elapsed time.

Affect appropriate overall, with situational distress when recalling specific parts of the journey. Reports intrusive sensations of persistent burden and of being watched, both improving but not fully resolved.

assessment.diagnosis: Traumatic amputation of right ring finger
